types.embedding_query_text: Country: A nation or state, typically occupying a particular territory and having its own government. Also called Nation, State, Realm, Land. Examples: Democratic Republic of Congo, Belgium, UK, Uganda.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/Country perfectly matches the definition and mentions for a nation or state.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: GovernmentOfficial
candidates.comment: A person holding an office or position in a government.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: Archipelago
candidates.comment: A group or chain of islands.

candidates.label: Embassy
candidates.comment: An Embassy is a GovernmentBuilding representing the diplomatic mission of one country in another. Also called consulate, diplomatic mission, high commission. Examples: The U.S. Embassy in London, the French Embassy in Washington D.C., a country's consulate general.

candidates.label: GroupOfPeople
candidates.comment: A collection of individuals.

candidates.label: GovernmentService
candidates.comment: A GovernmentService is an intangible service provided by a government organization to the public. Also called public service, state-provided service, municipal offering. Examples: food stamps program, veterans benefits, public education, waste collection.

types.embedding_query_text: Disease Outbreak: A sudden increase in the incidence of a disease in a particular area or population. Also called Epidemic, Infection surge, Disease flare-up. Examples: Ebola outbreak, current deadly Ebola outbreak, the disease, Ebola.

chosen_type.label: DiseaseOutbreak
chosen_type.definition: A sudden increase in the incidence of a disease in a particular area or population.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org or vocab type directly represents a 'Disease Outbreak' as an entity; it's a medical situation, not just a condition or event.

candidates.label: ExcessDeathsEvent
candidates.comment: An event characterized by a higher-than-expected number of deaths in a given period.

candidates.label: InfectiousDisease
candidates.comment: An InfectiousDisease is a medical condition resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents like viruses, bacteria, or fungi. Also called communicable disease, contagious illness, infection. Examples: influenza, COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis. Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is a broader category for any health problem.

candidates.label: WildfireEvent
candidates.comment: An event of uncontrolled fires in a natural area.

candidates.label: LocationType
candidates.comment: A classification for a kind of place or area.

candidates.label: CauseOfDeath
candidates.comment: The specific injury or disease that leads to death.

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: EventType
candidates.comment: A classification or category for a kind of event.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: Heatwave
candidates.comment: A prolonged period of abnormally hot weather.

candidates.label: Impact
candidates.comment: The effect or influence of one thing on another.

types.embedding_query_text: International Organization: An organization with an international membership, scope, or presence. Also called Global body, Multinational group, World agency. Examples: World Health Organization, WHO.

chosen_type.label: MedicalOrganization
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/MedicalOrganization explicitly lists 'World Health Organization' as an example and fits the international medical scope.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: NGO
candidates.comment: An NGO (Non-governmental Organization) is a non-profit organization that operates independently of any government. Also called non-profit organization, charity, civil society organization. Examples: Doctors Without Borders, Amnesty International, local community charity. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category including for-profit entities.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: Cooperative
candidates.comment: A Cooperative is an organization formed as a joint project by multiple organizations or individuals, often for mutual benefit. Also called member-owned business, co-op, collective. Examples: REI (Recreational Equipment, Inc.), Ocean Spray, Sunkist Growers, credit unions. Distinct from Corporation, which is a business entity owned by shareholders.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: MemberProgramTier
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status. Examples: "Gold Member", "Platinum Tier", "Basic Membership Level".

candidates.label: MemberProgram
candidates.comment: An intangible loyalty or membership program that offers specific benefits to its members. Also called loyalty program, membership scheme, rewards program. Examples: an airline frequent flyer program, a supermarket loyalty card, a gym membership.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: A human being as an individual. Also called Individual, Human, Man, Woman, Child. Examples: patient, pregnant woman, individual, first patient.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/Person is the direct and perfect match for a human being as an individual.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: ImportantPerson
candidates.comment: An individual recognized for their high status, influence, or celebrity.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: PeopleAudience
candidates.comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: GroupOfPeople
candidates.comment: A collection of individuals.

candidates.label: Patient
candidates.comment: A Patient, as a MedicalAudience, is any person receiving health care services. Also called healthcare recipient, medical client, care receiver. Examples: a person visiting a doctor for a check-up, someone undergoing surgery, a person receiving therapy. Distinct from Physician, who provides medical care.

candidates.label: Characteristic
candidates.comment: A distinguishing quality or attribute of a person or thing.

types.embedding_query_text: Official: A person holding an office or engaged in public service. Also called Dignitary, Administrator, Executive, Representative. Examples: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Dr Samuel Roger Kamba, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Tedros.

chosen_type.label: GovernmentOfficial
chosen_type.definition: A person holding an office or position in a government.
chosen_type.justification: vocab/GovernmentOfficial directly matches the definition and mentions for a person holding public office.

candidates.label: GovernmentOfficial
candidates.comment: A person holding an office or position in a government.

candidates.label: Representative
candidates.comment: A person or group acting on behalf of another person or entity.

candidates.label: GovernmentOffice
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOffice is a local business representing a specific governmental agency or department. Also called public agency office, state department branch, municipal service center. Examples: IRS office, DMV office, local planning department, social security office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is the physical structure that may contain multiple offices.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: Notary
candidates.comment: A Notary is a local business or individual providing legal services, specifically witnessing and authenticating signatures on documents. Also called notary public, public notary, legal witness. Examples: a notary service at a bank, an independent notary, a legal office offering notarization. Distinct from Lawyer, who provides broader legal counsel.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: GovernmentPermit
candidates.comment: A GovernmentPermit is a formal authorization issued by a government agency. Also called public license, state approval, official authorization. Examples: building permit, driver's license, business operating license, fishing permit.

candidates.label: Attorney
candidates.comment: An Attorney is a LegalService professional who practices law, providing legal advice and representation. Also called lawyer, legal counsel, barrister, solicitor. Examples: a criminal defense attorney, a corporate lawyer, a family law solicitor, a public defender. Distinct from LegalService, which is the broader category of services provided by legal professionals.

candidates.label: ImportantPerson
candidates.comment: An individual recognized for their high status, influence, or celebrity.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

types.embedding_query_text: DayOfWeek: A specific day within a calendar week. Also called Weekday, Weekend day, Calendar day. Examples: Thursday.

chosen_type.label: DayOfWeek
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/DayOfWeek is a direct and perfect match for a specific day within a calendar week.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: TimeOfDay
candidates.comment: A general period within a day, such as morning, afternoon, or night.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: HolidayWeekend
candidates.comment: A weekend extended by a public holiday.

candidates.label: Year
candidates.comment: A specific calendar year.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: DateRange
candidates.comment: A specified period of time between a start and end date.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

types.embedding_query_text: Quantity: A measurable amount or number of something. Also called Amount, Number, Count, Volume. Examples: 1,400 cases, 438 deaths, 1,460 confirmed cases, 150 suspected cases.

chosen_type.label: Quantity
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/Quantity is the most appropriate type for measurable amounts like '1,400 cases' or '438 deaths'.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: StatisticalVariable
candidates.comment: A measurable statistical metric that can be observed at a place and time, defined by a population type and specific constraints. Also called statistical metric, data point, observable quantity, measurement variable. Examples: median height of female persons, average temperature in a city, count of news articles published daily. Distinct from StatisticalPopulation, which is the group being measured, not the measurement itself.

candidates.label: Distance
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

candidates.label: Energy
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Energy represents a numerical value combined with a unit of energy. Also called power, work, heat. Examples: "100 kWh", "500 Joules", "200 Calories", "1.21 Gigawatts".

candidates.label: TypeAndQuantityNode
candidates.comment: A structured value indicating the quantity, unit of measurement, and business function of goods within a bundle offer. Also called quantity specification, offer item details, bundle component. Examples: "3 kg of apples for sale", "2 units of product X as a bonus", "1 liter of milk in a grocery bundle".

candidates.label: Integer
candidates.comment: Integer is a data type representing a whole number without a fractional component. Also called whole number, natural number (if positive), counting number. Examples: 0, 1, -5, 1000. Distinct from Float, which includes decimal values.

candidates.label: Rate
candidates.comment: A measure, quantity, or frequency, typically one measured against another quantity or measure.

candidates.label: Percentage
candidates.comment: A rate, number, or amount expressed as a fraction of one hundred.

types.embedding_query_text: Virus Species: A specific classification of a virus, often characterized by genetic and phenotypic properties. Also called Viral type, Virus strain, Pathogen species. Examples: Bundibugyo virus species.

chosen_type.label: Taxon
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/Taxon is suitable for a specific biological classification like a 'virus species'.

candidates.label: InfectiousAgentClass
candidates.comment: InfectiousAgentClass is a medical enumeration of classes of agents or pathogens that transmit infectious diseases. Also called pathogen type, disease agent category, microbial class. Examples: 'Bacteria', 'Virus', 'Fungus', 'Parasite'.

candidates.label: Taxon
candidates.comment: A cohesive biological unit representing a group of organisms, such as a species, genus, or family. Also called biological classification, taxonomic group, species, genus. Examples: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris, Felidae (cat family), Plantae (plant kingdom).

candidates.label: EventType
candidates.comment: A classification or category for a kind of event.

candidates.label: DocumentType
candidates.comment: A classification for a kind of written or electronic record.

candidates.label: LocationType
candidates.comment: A classification for a kind of place or area.

candidates.label: VehicleType
candidates.comment: A classification for a kind of vehicle.

candidates.label: Gene
candidates.comment: A Gene is a BioChemEntity representing a discrete unit of inheritance that affects one or more biological traits. Also called genetic unit, hereditary factor. Examples: FOXP2, SCARNA21, the gene for eye color, a specific allele.

candidates.label: InfectiousDisease
candidates.comment: An InfectiousDisease is a medical condition resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents like viruses, bacteria, or fungi. Also called communicable disease, contagious illness, infection. Examples: influenza, COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis. Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is a broader category for any health problem.

candidates.label: USNonprofitType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United States. Also called US charity type, American non-profit category, US voluntary sector classification. Examples: a 501(c)(3) organization, a public charity, a private foundation.

candidates.label: Class
candidates.comment: An intangible concept representing a category or type of entity, equivalent to rdfs:Class. Also called type, category, kind, schema. Examples: "Person" class, "Product" class, "Event" class. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a specific term within a vocabulary.

types.embedding_query_text: Medical Product: Any substance or device used for medical purposes, such as diagnosis, treatment, or prevention of disease. Also called Pharmaceutical, Drug, Therapeutic, Medicine. Examples: vaccines, treatments, antiviral drugs, therapeutics.

chosen_type.label: MedicalProduct
chosen_type.definition: Any substance or device used for medical purposes, such as diagnosis, treatment, or prevention of disease.
chosen_type.justification: No single existing type covers the broad range of 'Medical Product' (vaccines, treatments, drugs) as a product; schema.org/Product is the best parent.

candidates.label: Drug
candidates.comment: A Drug is a Product that is a chemical or biological substance used as a medical therapy, having a physiological effect on an organism. Also called medicine, pharmaceutical, medication. Examples: Aspirin, Insulin, Penicillin, Ibuprofen.

candidates.label: MedicalDevicePurpose
candidates.comment: An enumeration of categories for medical devices, organized by their purpose or intended use. Also called device use, medical equipment function, intended purpose. Examples: "Diagnostic", "Therapeutic", "Surgical", "Monitoring".

candidates.label: MedicalTherapy
candidates.comment: A therapeutic medical procedure designed to prevent, treat, and cure human diseases and medical conditions. Also called medical treatment, healthcare intervention, therapy regimen. Examples: "pharmacotherapy", "behavioral therapy", "supportive therapy", "dialysis". Distinct from MedicalProcedure, which is a broader category including diagnostic procedures.

candidates.label: TreatmentIndication
candidates.comment: A medical indication specifying the appropriate use of a treatment for an underlying health condition or symptom. Also called therapeutic indication, medical use, treatment rationale. Examples: an antibiotic indicated for bacterial infections, a pain reliever indicated for headaches, a specific therapy for cancer.

candidates.label: PreventionIndication
candidates.comment: A PreventionIndication is a MedicalIndication for preventing an underlying medical condition, symptom, or disease. Also called prophylactic indication, preventative use. Examples: a vaccine for measles prevention, a medication to prevent migraines, dietary changes to prevent heart disease, exercise to prevent diabetes.

candidates.label: MedicalDevice
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any object used in a medical capacity for diagnosing or treating a patient. Also called medical instrument, healthcare apparatus, diagnostic tool. Examples: a stethoscope, an MRI machine, a surgical scalpel, a blood pressure monitor.

candidates.label: MedicalProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing a process of care, invasive or non-invasive, used for diagnostic, therapeutic, preventive, or palliative purposes. Also called medical intervention, clinical procedure, healthcare process. Examples: "surgery", "biopsy", "vaccination", "physical therapy".

candidates.label: DietarySupplement
candidates.comment: A product taken orally that contains dietary ingredients intended to supplement the diet, such as vitamins, minerals, or herbs. Also called Nutritional supplement, health supplement, vitamin, herbal remedy. Examples: Multivitamin pills, fish oil capsules, protein powder, ginseng extract. Distinct from Drug, which is primarily for treating, preventing, or diagnosing disease.

candidates.label: MedicalIndication
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing a condition or factor that suggests the use of a medical therapy. Also called indication for treatment, therapeutic rationale, medical justification. Examples: "high blood pressure" as an indication for antihypertensive drugs, "fever" as an indication for antipyretics.

candidates.label: TherapeuticProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical procedure specifically intended to treat a health condition or improve a patient's well-being. Also called medical treatment, therapy, healing procedure. Examples: chemotherapy, physical therapy, surgical removal of a tumor.

types.embedding_query_text: Virus: A small infectious agent that replicates only inside the living cells of an organism. Also called Microbe, Pathogen, Germ. Examples: Ebola virus.

chosen_type.label: Taxon
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/Taxon is appropriate for a specific biological entity like 'Ebola virus', which can be classified taxonomically.

candidates.label: InfectiousAgentClass
candidates.comment: InfectiousAgentClass is a medical enumeration of classes of agents or pathogens that transmit infectious diseases. Also called pathogen type, disease agent category, microbial class. Examples: 'Bacteria', 'Virus', 'Fungus', 'Parasite'.

candidates.label: InfectiousDisease
candidates.comment: An InfectiousDisease is a medical condition resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents like viruses, bacteria, or fungi. Also called communicable disease, contagious illness, infection. Examples: influenza, COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis. Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is a broader category for any health problem.

candidates.label: MedicalCause
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing the causative agent(s) responsible for a pathophysiologic process leading to a medical condition, symptom, or sign. Also called etiology, causative factor, underlying reason. Examples: "HIV virus" as a cause of AIDS, "pulmonary embolism" as a cause of cardiac arrest, "bacterial infection".

candidates.label: Drug
candidates.comment: A Drug is a Product that is a chemical or biological substance used as a medical therapy, having a physiological effect on an organism. Also called medicine, pharmaceutical, medication. Examples: Aspirin, Insulin, Penicillin, Ibuprofen.

candidates.label: Label
candidates.comment: A small piece of material attached to an object, providing information.

candidates.label: Structure
candidates.comment: A building or other object constructed from several parts.

candidates.label: Taxon
candidates.comment: A cohesive biological unit representing a group of organisms, such as a species, genus, or family. Also called biological classification, taxonomic group, species, genus. Examples: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris, Felidae (cat family), Plantae (plant kingdom).

candidates.label: CauseOfDeath
candidates.comment: The specific injury or disease that leads to death.

candidates.label: Risk
candidates.comment: A situation involving exposure to danger.

candidates.label: Impact
candidates.comment: The effect or influence of one thing on another.

types.embedding_query_text: Research Institute: An establishment endowed for fundamental or applied research. Also called Research center, Laboratory, Scientific institution. Examples: Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale, Institute of Tropical Medicine.

chosen_type.label: ResearchOrganization
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/ResearchOrganization perfectly matches the definition and mentions for an establishment dedicated to research.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: ResearchProject
candidates.comment: A ResearchProject is a Project representing a planned enterprise aimed at scientific or academic inquiry. Also called research initiative, study, academic project. Examples: a clinical trial, a grant-funded scientific study, a historical research project, a university-led exploration.

candidates.label: Researcher
candidates.comment: A Researcher is an Audience type representing individuals engaged in scientific or academic inquiry. Also called scientist, academic, scholar. Examples: a university professor, a lab scientist, a PhD student, an independent scholar.

candidates.label: EducationalOrganization
candidates.comment: An EducationalOrganization is a CivicStructure that provides education. Also called learning institution, academic body, school. Examples: A university, a high school, a vocational college, a research institute.

candidates.label: FundingAgency
candidates.comment: A FundingAgency is an Organization that implements FundingSchemes and manages the granting process for projects and activities. Also called grant agency, funding body, research council. Examples: National Institutes of Health (NIH), European Research Council (ERC), Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation.

candidates.label: CollegeOrUniversity
candidates.comment: A third-level educational institution providing higher education. Also called university, college, higher education institution. Examples: Harvard University, Oxford College, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Sorbonne University. Distinct from EducationalOrganization, which is a broader category for any educational body.

candidates.label: MedicalStudy
candidates.comment: A medical entity that is an umbrella type covering all kinds of research studies relating to human medicine or health. Also called clinical study, health research, medical investigation. Examples: a drug trial, an epidemiological survey, a patient registry. Distinct from MedicalScholarlyArticle, which is the publication of study results, not the study itself.

candidates.label: DiagnosticLab
candidates.comment: A medical organization that provides on-site or off-site diagnostic services, such as testing and analysis. Also called Medical laboratory, pathology lab, clinical lab, testing facility. Examples: Quest Diagnostics, LabCorp, a hospital's pathology department. Distinct from MedicalClinic, which provides direct patient care and consultations.

candidates.label: ScholarlyArticle
candidates.comment: A formal article presenting original research or analysis, typically peer-reviewed and published in an academic journal. Also called academic paper, research article, journal publication, scientific paper. Examples: a paper published in Nature, a research article in the Journal of Marketing, a thesis chapter.

candidates.label: Museum
candidates.comment: A Museum is a civic structure dedicated to preserving and exhibiting artifacts, art, or scientific specimens. Also called gallery, exhibition hall, cultural institution. Examples: The Louvre, Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History, local art gallery. Distinct from Library, which primarily lends books and media.

types.embedding_query_text: University: An institution of higher education and research, which grants academic degrees in various subjects. Also called College, Academy, Higher education institution. Examples: University of Oxford.

chosen_type.label: CollegeOrUniversity
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/CollegeOrUniversity is a direct and perfect match for a higher education institution like 'University of Oxford'.

candidates.label: CollegeOrUniversity
candidates.comment: A third-level educational institution providing higher education. Also called university, college, higher education institution. Examples: Harvard University, Oxford College, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Sorbonne University. Distinct from EducationalOrganization, which is a broader category for any educational body.

candidates.label: EducationalOrganization
candidates.comment: An EducationalOrganization is a CivicStructure that provides education. Also called learning institution, academic body, school. Examples: A university, a high school, a vocational college, a research institute.

candidates.label: School
candidates.comment: An educational organization providing instruction to students, typically for primary or secondary education. Also called educational institution, academy, learning center, college. Examples: a public elementary school, a private high school, a vocational school, a university.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization

candidates.comment: A FundingAgency is an Organization that implements FundingSchemes and manages the granting process for projects and activities. Also called grant agency, funding body, research council. Examples: National Institutes of Health (NIH), European Research Council (ERC), Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation.

types.embedding_query_text: Province: A principal administrative division of certain countries or empires. Also called Region, State, Territory, Department. Examples: South Kivu, North Kivu, Ituri, Tshopo province.

chosen_type.label: State
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/State explicitly includes 'province' in its definition and is a perfect match for administrative divisions.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: GovernmentOffice
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOffice is a local business representing a specific governmental agency or department. Also called public agency office, state department branch, municipal service center. Examples: IRS office, DMV office, local planning department, social security office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is the physical structure that may contain multiple offices.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: Continent
candidates.comment: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.

candidates.label: SchoolDistrict
candidates.comment: An administrative area responsible for the organization and operation of public schools within its geographical boundaries. Also called education district, school system, local education authority. Examples: 'Los Angeles Unified School District', 'New York City Department of Education', 'Springfield School District 186'.

candidates.label: TouristDestination
candidates.comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.

types.embedding_query_text: News Agency: An organization that gathers news reports and sells them to subscribing news organizations. Also called Press agency, Wire service, News bureau. Examples: Reuters, AFP.

chosen_type.label: NewsMediaOrganization
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/NewsMediaOrganization explicitly includes 'news agency' in its definition and is a perfect match.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: AskPublicNewsArticle
candidates.comment: An AskPublicNewsArticle is a NewsArticle that serves as an open call from a news organization, soliciting input, insights, or documentation from the public for reporting purposes. Also called public appeal article, crowdsourced news request, call for information. Examples: a newspaper asking readers for stories about a local event, a news site requesting photos from a natural disaster, a journalist seeking expert opinions on a topic.

candidates.label: GroupOfPeople
candidates.comment: A collection of individuals.

candidates.label: NewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle, as an Article, is a creative work whose content reports news or provides background context for understanding news. Also called news report, news story, journalistic article. Examples: a breaking news report, an investigative journalism piece, an opinion column in a newspaper. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically less formal and often personal.

candidates.label: ReportageNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A ReportageNewsArticle is a NewsArticle representing news articles based on factual journalistic reporting, emphasizing verified information and multiple viewpoints. Also called news report, journalistic article, factual news. Examples: a breaking news story about a political event, an investigative report on a social issue, a factual account of a natural disaster, a report on scientific findings. Distinct from AnalysisNewsArticle, which goes deeper into analysis.

candidates.label: TelevisionStation
candidates.comment: A local business or organization that broadcasts television programs. Also called TV broadcaster, broadcast station, local TV channel. Examples: 'WNBC (New York)', 'BBC Television Centre', a local news station.

candidates.label: RadioStation
candidates.comment: A RadioStation is a LocalBusiness representing an organization that broadcasts radio content. Also called radio broadcaster, radio company. Examples: WNYC, BBC Radio, a local commercial radio station, a public radio station.

candidates.label: LawEnforcementOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization or group responsible for enforcing laws and maintaining order.

candidates.label: RadioBroadcastService
candidates.comment: A RadioBroadcastService is a BroadcastService delivering radio content via broadcast over the air or online. Also called radio service, broadcast radio. Examples: BBC Radio 4, NPR, a local FM radio station, an internet radio stream.

candidates.label: WorkersUnion
candidates.comment: An organization that advocates for the interests of its worker members through collective bargaining and political lobbying. Also called labor union, trade union, industrial union. Examples: United Auto Workers (UAW), National Education Association (NEA), a local plumbers' union.

types.embedding_query_text: Medical Facility: A place where medical care is provided, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called Healthcare center, Clinic, Hospital, Infirmary. Examples: isolation unit.

chosen_type.label: MedicalClinic
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/MedicalClinic's definition includes 'medical facility' and is a good fit for an 'isolation unit'.

candidates.label: MedicalClinic
candidates.comment: A medical business facility, often associated with a hospital, dedicated to specific diagnosis and/or healthcare, typically for outpatients but sometimes inpatients. Also called clinic, healthcare center, medical facility. Examples: a dermatology clinic, a walk-in clinic, a university health clinic, a family practice. Distinct from Hospital, which is a larger institution providing comprehensive medical care.

candidates.label: Hospital
candidates.comment: A Hospital is a civic structure and medical institution providing patient treatment with specialized medical and nursing staff and equipment. Also called medical center, clinic, healthcare facility. Examples: Mayo Clinic, Massachusetts General Hospital, a local emergency room.

candidates.label: PhysiciansOffice
candidates.comment: A PhysiciansOffice, as a Physician, is a doctor's office or clinic where medical consultations and treatments are provided. Also called doctor's clinic, medical office, medical practice. Examples: a family doctor's practice, a specialist's clinic, an urgent care center. Distinct from Hospital, which offers inpatient care and emergency services.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: MedicalBusiness
candidates.comment: A local business operating for medical purposes, which can be physical or virtual. Also called healthcare business, medical practice, health services provider. Examples: a dental office, a physical therapy clinic, a telemedicine service, a diagnostic lab. Distinct from LocalBusiness, which is a broader category for any local business.

candidates.label: DiagnosticLab
candidates.comment: A medical organization that provides on-site or off-site diagnostic services, such as testing and analysis. Also called Medical laboratory, pathology lab, clinical lab, testing facility. Examples: Quest Diagnostics, LabCorp, a hospital's pathology department. Distinct from MedicalClinic, which provides direct patient care and consultations.

candidates.label: VeterinaryCare
candidates.comment: A local business or organization providing medical services for animals. Also called vet clinic, animal hospital, veterinary practice. Examples: a local veterinary office, an emergency animal hospital, a mobile vet service.

candidates.label: Physician
candidates.comment: A Physician, as a MedicalBusiness, is an individual doctor or a doctor's office considered as a MedicalOrganization. Also called doctor, medical practitioner, medical doctor. Examples: a general practitioner, a specialist physician, a family doctor's clinic. Distinct from Hospital, which is a larger medical facility.

candidates.label: MedicalEntity
candidates.comment: The most generic type of entity related to health and the practice of medicine. Also called healthcare entity, medical concept, health-related item. Examples: a disease, a drug, a doctor, a medical procedure, a hospital. Distinct from Thing, which is the root of all schema.org types.

candidates.label: MedicalDevice
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any object used in a medical capacity for diagnosing or treating a patient. Also called medical instrument, healthcare apparatus, diagnostic tool. Examples: a stethoscope, an MRI machine, a surgical scalpel, a blood pressure monitor.

types.embedding_query_text: DateRange: A period of time spanning multiple days, weeks, or months. Also called Timeframe, Period, Interval. Examples: Earlier this week.

chosen_type.label: DateRange
chosen_type.definition: A specified period of time between a start and end date.
chosen_type.justification: vocab/DateRange is a direct and perfect match for a period of time spanning multiple days, weeks, or months.

candidates.label: DateRange
candidates.comment: A specified period of time between a start and end date.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: AgeRange
candidates.comment: A span of years indicating a person's age.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: TimeOfDay
candidates.comment: A general period within a day, such as morning, afternoon, or night.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

types.embedding_query_text: Social Event: An organized occasion for people to gather and interact. Also called Gathering, Assembly, Public meeting. Examples: public gatherings.

chosen_type.label: SocialEvent
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/SocialEvent is a direct and perfect match for an organized occasion for people to gather and interact, like 'public gatherings'.

candidates.label: SocialEvent
candidates.comment: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.

candidates.label: DanceEvent
candidates.comment: A DanceEvent is a social gathering or organized occasion primarily focused on dancing. Also called dance party, ball, disco, social dance. Examples: A salsa night, a wedding reception with dancing, a school prom, a folk dance festival.

candidates.label: BusinessEvent
candidates.comment: A BusinessEvent is an Event related to commercial activities, such as conferences, trade shows, or corporate meetings. Also called corporate event, professional gathering, industry event. Examples: a sales conference, a product launch event, an annual shareholder meeting. Distinct from SocialEvent, which is for personal or recreational gatherings.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: ChildrensEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized and designed for children. Also called kids' event, family event, youth gathering. Examples: A puppet show, a children's birthday party, a school play, a kids' festival.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: InteractAction
candidates.comment: An InteractAction is an action representing the act of interacting with another person or organization. Also called engagement action, social action, communication action. Examples: communicating, joining, inviting, following. Distinct from CommunicateAction, which is a specific type of interaction focused on information exchange.

candidates.label: Festival
candidates.comment: A Festival is an Event that is a public celebration or series of special events. Also called celebration, gala, fete. Examples: A music festival, a film festival, a cultural heritage festival, a food and wine festival.

candidates.label: EventSeries
candidates.comment: An EventSeries is an Event representing a collection of events that share unifying characteristics, such as a recurring festival or a thematic lecture series. Also called event cycle, recurring event, series of events. Examples: The Olympic Games, a monthly book club meeting, a season of a concert series, a weekly farmers market.

candidates.label: EventVenue
candidates.comment: An EventVenue is a CivicStructure that serves as a location for events. Also called venue, event space, performance hall. Examples: A concert hall, a stadium, a conference center, a community hall.

types.embedding_query_text: Disease: A disorder of structure or function in a human, animal, or plant, especially one that produces specific symptoms or that affects a specific location and is not simply a direct result of physical injury. Also called Illness, Sickness, Ailment. Examples: flu, malaria.

chosen_type.label: MedicalCondition
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/MedicalCondition is a direct and perfect match for a 'disease', explicitly listing 'influenza' (flu) as an example.

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: Structure
candidates.comment: A building or other object constructed from several parts.

candidates.label: CauseOfDeath
candidates.comment: The specific injury or disease that leads to death.

candidates.label: AnatomicalStructure
candidates.comment: An AnatomicalStructure is a MedicalEntity representing any part of the human body, such as organs, tissues, or cells. Also called body part, biological structure, anatomical component. Examples: The heart, a bone, a muscle, a neuron, the liver. Distinct from AnatomicalSystem, which is a group of structures working together.

candidates.label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical condition representing any feature, objective or subjective, associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical manifestation, health indicator, disease feature. Examples: "pain", "fever", "fatigue", "rash", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is the underlying state itself.

candidates.label: InfectiousDisease
candidates.comment: An InfectiousDisease is a medical condition resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents like viruses, bacteria, or fungi. Also called communicable disease, contagious illness, infection. Examples: influenza, COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis. Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is a broader category for any health problem.

candidates.label: SuperficialAnatomy
candidates.comment: Anatomical features observable by sight without dissection, including body form, proportions, and surface landmarks corresponding to deeper structures. Also called surface anatomy, external anatomy, visible body structures. Examples: the visible edges of the scapula, the cubital fossa for vein location, the contours of muscles under the skin.

candidates.label: House
candidates.comment: A House is an accommodation type representing a building or structure intended for human or other creature habitation. Also called dwelling, residence, home. Examples: a single-family home, a townhouse, a cottage. Distinct from Apartment, which is a unit within a larger building, and HotelRoom, which is a temporary lodging unit.

candidates.label: Bone
candidates.comment: An AnatomicalStructure consisting of rigid connective tissue that forms the skeletal structure of a body. Also called skeletal bone, osseous tissue. Examples: "Femur", "Skull bone", "Rib cage", "Vertebra". Distinct from Muscle, which is soft tissue for movement.

candidates.label: MedicalConditionStage
candidates.comment: A medical intangible representing a specific stage of a medical condition. Also called disease stage, condition phase, severity level. Examples: "Stage IIIa cancer", "early-stage Alzheimer's", "acute phase of an infection".

types.embedding_query_text: Symptom: A physical or mental feature that is regarded as indicating a condition of disease, particularly such a feature that is apparent to the patient. Also called Sign, Indicator, Manifestation. Examples: fever, headache, tiredness.

chosen_type.label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/MedicalSignOrSymptom is a direct and perfect match for a 'symptom', explicitly listing 'fever' and 'headache' as examples.

candidates.label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical condition representing any feature, objective or subjective, associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical manifestation, health indicator, disease feature. Examples: "pain", "fever", "fatigue", "rash", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is the underlying state itself.

candidates.label: MedicalSign
candidates.comment: A medical sign or symptom that is an objective physical manifestation of a medical condition, discoverable by diagnostic tests or physical examination. Also called objective symptom, clinical sign, diagnostic finding. Examples: "fever", "rash", "high blood pressure", "swelling". Distinct from MedicalSymptom, which is subjective and reported by the patient.

candidates.label: MedicalSymptom
candidates.comment: A medical sign or symptom that is a subjective complaint sensed and expressed by the patient. Also called subjective symptom, patient complaint, reported feeling. Examples: "stomachache", "lower-back pain", "fatigue", "headache", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalSign, which is an objective finding.

candidates.label: VitalSign
candidates.comment: A measurable physiological function used to assess the most basic body functions and overall health. Also called physiological sign, health indicator, body function measure. Examples: body temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate.

candidates.label: MedicalIndication
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing a condition or factor that suggests the use of a medical therapy. Also called indication for treatment, therapeutic rationale, medical justification. Examples: "high blood pressure" as an indication for antihypertensive drugs, "fever" as an indication for antipyretics.

candidates.label: TreatmentIndication
candidates.comment: A medical indication specifying the appropriate use of a treatment for an underlying health condition or symptom. Also called therapeutic indication, medical use, treatment rationale. Examples: an antibiotic indicated for bacterial infections, a pain reliever indicated for headaches, a specific therapy for cancer.

candidates.label: MedicalConditionStage
candidates.comment: A medical intangible representing a specific stage of a medical condition. Also called disease stage, condition phase, severity level. Examples: "Stage IIIa cancer", "early-stage Alzheimer's", "acute phase of an infection".

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: PreventionIndication
candidates.comment: A PreventionIndication is a MedicalIndication for preventing an underlying medical condition, symptom, or disease. Also called prophylactic indication, preventative use. Examples: a vaccine for measles prevention, a medication to prevent migraines, dietary changes to prevent heart disease, exercise to prevent diabetes.

candidates.label: MedicalCause
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing the causative agent(s) responsible for a pathophysiologic process leading to a medical condition, symptom, or sign. Also called etiology, causative factor, underlying reason. Examples: "HIV virus" as a cause of AIDS, "pulmonary embolism" as a cause of cardiac arrest, "bacterial infection".

types.embedding_query_text: Organization Group: A collection of multiple organizations or entities. Also called Consortium, Alliance, Network. Examples: International organisations.

chosen_type.label: Consortium
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/Consortium is a good fit for a group of organizations collaborating, which 'International organisations' often do.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: Cooperative
candidates.comment: A Cooperative is an organization formed as a joint project by multiple organizations or individuals, often for mutual benefit. Also called member-owned business, co-op, collective. Examples: REI (Recreational Equipment, Inc.), Ocean Spray, Sunkist Growers, credit unions. Distinct from Corporation, which is a business entity owned by shareholders.

candidates.label: LibrarySystem
candidates.comment: A LibrarySystem is an organization representing a collaborative network or system among several libraries. Also called library consortium, library network, regional library system. Examples: a state library system, a university library consortium, a public library district. Distinct from Library, which is a single physical or organizational entity.

candidates.label: GroupOfPeople
candidates.comment: A collection of individuals.

candidates.label: NGO
candidates.comment: An NGO (Non-governmental Organization) is a non-profit organization that operates independently of any government. Also called non-profit organization, charity, civil society organization. Examples: Doctors Without Borders, Amnesty International, local community charity. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category including for-profit entities.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: Collection
candidates.comment: A grouping of various items, which can include creative works or products. Also called assortment, compilation, set, aggregate. Examples: A collection of rare books, a stamp collection, a music album, a product catalog.

types.embedding_query_text: Conflict: A serious disagreement or argument, typically a protracted one, often involving armed struggle. Also called Dispute, Strife, Warfare, Hostilities. Examples: conflict in eastern DR Congo.

chosen_type.label: ConflictEvent
chosen_type.definition: A serious disagreement or argument, typically a protracted one, often involving armed struggle.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org or vocab type directly represents a 'Conflict' as a protracted event or situation; schema.org/Event is the best parent.

candidates.label: DisagreeAction
candidates.comment: A react action expressing a negative opinion or difference of opinion regarding an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express disagreement, object to, dispute, dissent. Examples: Disagreeing with a political statement, objecting to a proposed plan, disputing a fact. Distinct from AgreeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or agreement.

candidates.label: Descriptor
candidates.comment: A word or phrase used to describe something.

candidates.label: Preference
candidates.comment: A greater liking for one alternative over another or others.

candidates.label: ExcessDeathsEvent
candidates.comment: An event characterized by a higher-than-expected number of deaths in a given period.

candidates.label: EventType
candidates.comment: A classification or category for a kind of event.

candidates.label: GroupOfPeople
candidates.comment: A collection of individuals.

candidates.label: Impact
candidates.comment: The effect or influence of one thing on another.

candidates.label: EvacuationEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving the movement of people from a dangerous place to safety.

candidates.label: Risk
candidates.comment: A situation involving exposure to danger.

candidates.label: Opinion
candidates.comment: A view or judgment formed about something, not necessarily based on fact or knowledge.

types.embedding_query_text: Rebel Group: An organized group that resists the government or ruling power, often through armed rebellion. Also called Insurgent group, Militia, Guerrilla force. Examples: M23 rebel group.

chosen_type.label: RebelGroup
chosen_type.definition: An organized group that resists the government or ruling power, often through armed rebellion.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org or vocab type directly represents a 'Rebel Group'; schema.org/Organization is the best parent.

candidates.label: LawEnforcementOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization or group responsible for enforcing laws and maintaining order.

candidates.label: GovernmentOfficial
candidates.comment: A person holding an office or position in a government.

candidates.label: PoliticalParty
candidates.comment: A PoliticalParty is an Organization formed to contest elections and hold power in government. Also called political movement, party. Examples: Democratic Party, Republican Party, Labour Party, Conservative Party.

candidates.label: GroupOfPeople
candidates.comment: A collection of individuals.

candidates.label: Archipelago
candidates.comment: A group or chain of islands.

candidates.label: Structure
candidates.comment: A building or other object constructed from several parts.

candidates.label: Photographer
candidates.comment: An individual who takes photographs.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: Month
candidates.comment: One of the twelve divisions of the year.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.
